subject: Private deployment: operator demarcation, customer keys, and cross-border transfer flags
messages:
From: Anna Cho <anna@helixmed.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: HelixMed Security <security@helixmed.com>, HelixMed Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on private deployment operator access & keys

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. We reviewed the draft DPA annex and have a handful of follow-ups specific to the Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) option:

- Customer key custody: We want confirmation that the CMK can be HSM-backed and customer-controlled (no operator escrow by default). If operator break-glass is required, what governance & audit steps will Redwood follow?
- Operator vs Redwood-managed processes: What exact telemetry/metrics will your ops team see if we run the private control plane in our VPC? Any chance raw prompts or model outputs leave our network?
- Subprocessors: Please provide an explicit list for the on-prem install pattern (support engineers, monitoring vendors, infra partners).
- Cross-border concerns: If support access is needed, will logs/telemetry cross borders? We have EU patients and prefer all telemetry to remain within US/EU as applicable.

I've attached HelixMed_DPA_QA_v2.pdf with redlines. Could we get a short doc that maps each of our asks to the proposed technical and contract controls? If helpful, happy to schedule a 30-min call next week.

Thanks,
Anna Cho
Head of Security, HelixMed
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Anna Cho <anna@helixmed.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment operator access & keys

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list and the redlines. Quick answers up front and then I attached a short annex with mapping: redwood-privdep-annex.docx.

- CMK ownership: We support HSM-backed customer CMKs (Cloud KMS/HSM or on-prem HSM). By default keys are customer-managed; Redwood does not escrow CMKs.
- Break-glass: Operator break-glass is available only under emergency procedures documented in the annex: 2-person approval (manager + security lead), signed request, time-limited access token, and recorded session logs. We will not have plaintext key material — any operator actions are via audited key wrapping APIs and require explicit customer authorization except in narrowly-defined emergency clauses.
- Telemetry: Ops receive aggregated health metrics and anonymized performance telemetry (e.g., GPU utilization, queue depth). We do not transmit raw prompt or model output from the VPC. App-level traces can be collected only if customer enables them and opts into sharing; they can be configured to scrub user data.
- Subprocessors: For private deployments the list is shorter; core subprocessors (support engineers, monitoring vendor) are listed in section 3 of the annex. We'll provide full names and country of processing.
- Cross-border: Logs/telemetry follow the routing policy you pick (us/eu/apac). By default, diagnostic payloads are kept in-region; any cross-border transfer for support requires explicit consent and is logged.

Proposed next step: 30-min legal+security call Monday 26th or Tuesday 27th. If Monday works, we'll include Kim (legal) and Rishi (security ops).

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Product Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-privdep-annex.docx (contains mapping table and operator controls)
From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Anna Cho <anna@helixmed.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment operator access & keys

Anna — adding legal detail inline based on your redlines. A few items we should confirm in contract language:

1) 'Operator access' definition — we propose: temporary privileged access granted only for the narrow purpose of provisioning, emergency remediation, or security patching; explicitly excludes data exfiltration or content inspection.
2) Break-glass governance — proposed clause: operator access requires (a) customer-signed request, (b) approval from Redwood Security Lead and Customer Security Owner, (c) 2FA-enabled session, (d) time-limited SAB token automatically destroyed after use. All sessions recorded and retained per the retention schedule in Exhibit B.
3) Subprocessor transparency — add obligation to notify customer 30 days before onboarding new subprocessor for private deployments, with right to object for lawful data residency reasons.
4) Escrow exceptions — escrow only for disaster recovery if both parties sign an evac authorization and escrow is strictly encrypted and accessible only to named custodians.

I've drafted contract text and included a suggested Exhibit B for logs retention in the annex. If HelixMed wants a tighter retention window we can propose SOW pricing for shorter retention or zero-retain telemetry mode.

- Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Trust, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-dpa-clause-snippets.txt (in annex)
From: Anna Cho <anna@helixmed.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: HelixMed Security <security@helixmed.com>, HelixMed Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment operator access & keys

Thanks Naomi and Kim — that mapping is helpful. A couple of follow-ups after internal review:

- Dual-approval for break-glass: We prefer a 2-of-3 approval model where at least one approver must be from the customer's security team. Can Redwood support that operationally?
- Telemetry retention: HelixMed's policy is 90 days for infra telemetry; do you have a zero-retain option for sensitive workloads (i.e., metrics only in-memory and never persisted)? If so, what's the perf/operational tradeoff?
- Subprocessor list: Please include the country for each subprocessor and the role (support, monitoring, or infra).

Procurement also flagged the timeline: we'd like final DPA language + SOW by May 10 to stay on our Q3 deployment cadence.

— Anna
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Anna Cho <anna@helixmed.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment operator access & keys

Hi Anna — quick confirmation and concrete proposal so procurement and security can move forward:

1) Break-glass approvals: We can support a 2-of-3 approval model operationally. Proposed approvers: Redwood Security Lead, Redwood Ops Manager, and HelixMed Security Owner. At least one approver must be HelixMed. Approval workflow will be logged and appended to the ticket; we can include the audit trail in Discovery logs.

2) Telemetry retention: We offer three modes:
   - Standard (default): aggregated metrics persisted for 180 days; anonymized by default.
   - Short-retain: 90 days (no charge for the change).
   - Ephemeral: in-memory-only metrics with no persistence (available as an add-on; note there is a small operational visibility cost: longer incident debug time and limited historical trend analysis).

3) Subprocessor disclosure: See attached kms-handshake-diagram.png and section 3 of the annex for the current roster with countries and roles. If HelixMed objects to any subprocessor for legal reasons, we will either (a) remove the subprocessor from HelixMed's deployment, or (b) offer an alternate approved partner; objection window is 30 days from notice.

4) Escrow & emergency: We remain aligned that Redwood will not hold customer key material. Escrow is only via customer-approved & mutually-signed escrow agreement and requires dual custody.

Next steps: I uploaded the proposed DPA snippets and annex to the DocuSign prep link: https://redwood.app/docusign/HLX-9271. If procurement confirms timeline, I'll route the DPA + SOW for signature by May 6.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Product Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: HelixMed_DPA_QA_v2.pdf, kms-handshake-diagram.png, redwood-privdep-annex.docx
